quotes.text: You can’t add funds to the customer cash balance directly.
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.
[Enable bank transfers](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods) as a payment method in your Dashboard before creating the intent.
The payment succeeds if the cash balance has sufficient funds, and fails otherwise.
Changes to the customer’s cash balance are modeled as a list of [cash balance transactions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/cash_balance_transactions/object.md).

old_evidence.text: To view the balance for a customer-configured `Account`, use the Customers API endpoint with the Account ID as the path parameter, for example `v1/customers/acct_xxxxx`.
The payment succeeds if the cash balance has sufficient funds, and fails otherwise.
| `transferred_to_balance` | Funds have been moved from the cash balance to your Stripe balance due to failed refunds or insufficient refund details.

findings: Cash balance and invoice balance remain distinct: unreconciled or excess bank-transfer funds enter the customer's per-currency cash balance for later payments to that same customer or return up to the available amount; it cannot be directly topped up or used as a wallet. Invoice balance is a liability/credit offset for future invoices, adjusted by Customer Balance Transactions, not spendable cash (old raw lines 8-20; new raw lines 9-21; source lines 17-19).

Viewing cash balance still means retrieving a Customer and expanding cash_balance, or viewing the Customer page. A customer-configured Account in Accounts v2 is addressed through the Customers API with its acct_ ID as path parameter; the new capture adds generally available Accounts v2 for Connect users versus public preview for others, with preview-version specification for preview participants. Do not collapse the v1 Customer and customer-configured Account identities or infer universal availability (old raw lines 22-37, 113; new raw lines 23-38, 123; source line 21).

Paying from available cash balance still uses a customer_balance PaymentIntent and sufficient funds; insufficient funds cause failure, with separate bank-transfer funding as a route for more funds. The new page explicitly says to enable bank transfers in Dashboard before intent creation, and its curl examples distinguish customer_account for Accounts v2 from customer for Customers v1. PaymentIntent creation/confirm=true and return_url in the illustrative request do not independently prove success or a redirect requirement; check actual intent state (old raw lines 115-165; new raw lines 125-167; source lines 23-33).

The seven cash-balance transaction types and their causes are unchanged: funded, applied_to_payment, unapplied_from_payment, refunded_from_payment, return_initiated, return_canceled and transferred_to_balance. Funded may auto-apply depending on reconciliation; return_initiated is not completed bank return, and transferred_to_balance refers to failed returns/insufficient details, not a merchant top-up path (old raw lines 167-185; new raw lines 169-187; source lines 35-45).

The source's line 49 labels the old raw as 186 lines, but the pinned old file is 185 lines. This is a pre-existing metadata error, distinct from the semantic change (source line 49; old raw lines 1-185).
substantive_changes: New Accounts v2 availability and preview-version qualifier scopes the already documented customer-configured Account lookup (old raw lines 22-26; new raw lines 23-31).
New explicit bank-transfer Dashboard enablement prerequisite before creating the cash-balance PaymentIntent (old raw lines 115-117; new raw lines 125-129).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the 2026-05-05 Node.js retrieval and PaymentIntent examples, including payment_method_types, as dated examples rather than treating their absence from the 2026-11-07 curl examples as proof of API removal or invalidity (old raw lines 28-37, 119-157; new raw lines 33-38, 131-159).
Preserve the same-customer, per-currency, no-direct-top-up and seven-transaction-type definitions because both captures retain them (old raw lines 8-20, 167-185; new raw lines 9-21, 169-187).
conflicts: The current source and concept state that Accounts v2 retrieval works but omit its distinct Connect-general-availability versus other-user-public-preview and preview-version conditions; qualify both routes (source line 21; wiki/concepts/stripe-customer-balance.md line 23; new raw lines 27-31).

The current source/concept payment snippet lacks the new Dashboard bank-transfer enablement prerequisite and can imply an unqualified immediate success; qualify it with sufficient available funds and actual PaymentIntent state (source lines 23-33; wiki/concepts/stripe-customer-balance.md line 25; new raw lines 125-167).

The old Node.js example includes payment_method_types while the new curl examples omit it; this is an example-language/shape difference, not evidence of a universally removed request field (old raw lines 127-156; new raw lines 135-159).
unresolved_questions: The two captures do not prove which particular account is in Accounts v2 preview, has bank transfers enabled, or has available cash balance; actual account and PaymentIntent states remain external to these snapshots (new raw lines 27-31, 125-167).

The overview's illustrative curl return_url does not explain whether a specific cash-balance payment flow redirects or what client return means for success; avoid inferring either from the sample alone (new raw lines 135-159).

findings: Add exact canonical URL and 2026-11-07 raw provenance while retaining the 2026-05-05 old raw; add Accounts v2 availability/preview-version qualifier and the bank-transfer Dashboard enablement prerequisite (source lines 1-13, 21-33, 47-49; new raw lines 1-2, 27-31, 125-129).

Keep cash/invoice distinctions and seven transaction types, with payment success conditioned on available funds and observed intent state (source lines 17-45; old raw lines 8-20, 159-185; new raw lines 9-21, 161-187).
conflicts: Existing unqualified Accounts v2 and payment code route omits newer availability and enablement prerequisites (source lines 21-33; new raw lines 27-31, 125-129).
The old raw line count in source line 49 is off by one (old raw lines 1-185).
source_assessments.reason: Two material documented prerequisites/availability qualifiers changed, and the existing source omits them despite otherwise accurately summarizing the stable balance model.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/customer-balance, the new capture continues to distinguish per-customer, per-currency cash balance created by unreconciled or excess bank transfers from invoice balance, an invoice-liability offset that cannot fund direct payments. Cash cannot be topped up or used as a wallet, and the seven cash-balance transaction types preserve their causes and state transitions (new raw lines 9-21, 169-187; old raw lines 8-20, 167-185). A Customer's cash_balance is retrieved with expansion; a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account uses its acct_ ID at the Customers endpoint, with Connect general availability, other-user public preview and a preview-version requirement for preview participants (new raw lines 23-31). A customer_balance PaymentIntent requires bank transfers enabled and succeeds only if sufficient cash is available (new raw lines 125-167). source-stripe-customer-balance.md covers the stable model but omits those new qualifiers and overstates the old file length (source lines 21-33, 49).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/customer-balance, the substantive additions are Accounts v2's Connect-versus-other-user availability and preview-version condition, plus explicit Dashboard bank-transfer enablement before creating an intent (new raw lines 27-31, 125-129; old raw lines 22-26, 115-117). The Node.js-to-curl switch, JSON whitespace and trailing commas, heading spaces and table formatting are presentation or example differences, and omission of payment_method_types in the curl sample does not repeal the older Node.js example (old raw lines 28-37, 119-157; new raw lines 33-121, 131-159). source-stripe-customer-balance.md should keep the 2026-05-05 Node.js material dated, add the new qualification and correct its line count. The customer_account versus customer parameters mark different account identities; confirm=true, return_url and a created PaymentIntent are not proof of a successful payment, refund completion, bank-transfer enablement or available funds.
